answer: To forge a second identity, an attacker must acquire duplicate hardware and burn equivalent compute per epoch, making sybil farms linearly costly rather than free. Each agent must solve a per-epoch proof-of-work keyed to a hardware quartz oscillator's timing jitter, producing a unique cipher signature that binds identity to physical entropy. Honest peers verify signatures cheaply, so fake identities fail attestation while real operators amortize cost across genuine work. From qwe0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
